Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

c4e (development version)

c4e is the successor of climatic4economist, started from its v2 redesign with the full history. climatic4economist 0.1 stays available unchanged for existing scripts. The design is in dev/PLAN_v2.md and progress is tracked in dev/LOG_v2.md.

Done so far

  • c4e_tbl tables carry their context (key, variable, unit, time step, dates, CRS, indicator registry, history); c4e_meta(), update_meta(), bind_indicators(), c4e_history().

  • Defaults are read from upstream and announced; large steps split by unit or by layer when they exceed the memory budget (options(c4e.mem_limit = )), with progress messages (options(c4e.verbose = )).

  • Units: convert_unit() for rasters and tables, including rates per day, month or year; register_unit(), list_units().

  • Rasters: read_climate(), raster_meta(), aggregate_time(), register_source(), list_sources(); select_by_dates() and select_by_season() work on rasters; read_boundaries().

  • Extraction returns c4e_tbl with the raster’s context, checks CRS, reports locations without data, buffers points and extracts in blocks of layers.

  • Daily indicators on a matrix kernel, equal to the v1 results and up to 900 times faster: calc_threshold_day(), calc_condition(), calc_percentile(), calc_percentile_day(), calc_spell(), calc_spell_percentile(), calc_spell_excess(), calc_heatwave().

  • Standardised indices and parameters: calc_std_index() (SPI and SPEI), calc_std_threshold(), and calc_par() with periods and coverage.

  • Survey side: stable coordinate IDs in prepare_coord(), window objects (window_lag(), window_season(), window_fixed(), window_since()), summarise_by_interview(), summarise_by_period(), aggregate_to_adm().

  • Export and inspection: write_stata() with variable labels and a codebook, c4e_labels(), validate_c4e(), summary().

  • Wrappers that run the whole chain in one call: weather_extremes(), climate_indices(), static_controls() and time_varying_controls(), with presets (list_presets()), a specification block, step progress, dry_run, keep_steps, and lists of surveys; options in extremes_control(), indices_control() and controls_control().

  • Every cell of a raster: grid_indicators() (the extremes of weather_extremes(), per year or month) and grid_controls() (population density within radii, climate normals, other layers) return rasters; calc_threshold_day(), calc_percentile(), calc_par() and calc_std_index() also take a SpatRaster. Rasters are processed in blocks of rows and can be written to GeoTIFF; extract_by_coord() and extract_by_poly() restore the indicator registry from the file’s tags.

  • The v1 functions that the new ones replace are removed, with no deprecation wrappers: climatic4economist 0.1 keeps them for existing scripts. Removed: find_extr_abs_day(), find_extr_rel_day(), find_extr_spell_rel(), find_spell(), find_wmo_heatwave(), calc_pct_day(), calc_pct_spell(), compute_spell(), compute_spi(), compute_spei(), compute_water_balance(), extr_std_index(), extr_day_index(), extr_spell_index(), extr_day_by_interview(), extr_spell_by_interview(), agg_to_adm_div(), aggregate_frequency(), ave_dist_2shp(), ave_point_density_2shp(), above_threshold(), below_threshold(), is_above(), is_below(), substitute_l(), substitute_u(), quantile_df(), quantile_na_check(), character_to_clock(), second_to_date(), is_date(), sort_date_columns(). No longer exported (used inside the package): filter_by_interview(), find_merge_var(), read_GAUL(), read_geoBoundaries(), sum_na_check(), mean_na_check(), max_na_check(), to_date(). data.table is no longer imported.

  • Lighter installation: sf, exactextractr and furrr move to Suggests and are asked for only by coverage-weighted extraction (extract_cell_by_poly(), extract_weighted_by_poly(), extract_by_poly(weights = "coverage")) and by .parallel = TRUE; stringi, tidyterra and raster are no longer used.

  • Every example runs on the bundled data; a pkgdown site with the reference grouped by task; GPL-2 licence text in LICENSE.md.

Planned

  • The quick start and canonical vignettes, the country case studies on the new names (now in case_studies/), and the first release.
